umi-stanford.description: UMI (Universal Manipulation Interface) from Stanford et al. is a 780 g handheld gripper with a ~$371 total BoM (including GoPro). Humans demonstrate directly with a 155° fisheye camera and side mirrors, recovering 6-DoF trajectories via SLAM for zero-shot robot transfer.
highlights: Pioneered robot-free handheld capture; 3D-printed gripper BoM is $73 (~$371 with GoPro)
Side mirrors provide implicit stereo depth while matching wrist-camera views
Enables zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer across robot arm brands
Open-source CAD, SLAM calibration and Diffusion Policy training code

specs.tracking_method: GoPro monocular fisheye + built-in IMU visual-inertial SLAM (ORB-SLAM3)
specs.sensors: GoPro 155° fisheye + side mirrors (implicit stereo) + gripper encoder
specs.output_data: Wrist RGB video + 6-DoF end-effector pose + gripper width

fastumi.description: FastUMI decouples pose tracking from scene capture using a RealSense T265 alongside a GoPro Hero 9, outputting real-time 6-DoF TCP trajectories without offline SLAM post-processing and powering the 600-hour FastUMI-100K dataset.
highlights: RealSense T265 outputs 6-DoF pose directly, eliminating offline SLAM pipelines
Factory-calibrated fingertip alignment for wired real-time plug-and-play capture
Powered the 600-hour FastUMI-100K open-source dataset
Hardware-independent design compatible with diverse robot arms and grippers

specs.tracking_method: Intel RealSense T265 real-time 6-DoF VIO tracking
specs.output_data: 60 fps wrist fisheye RGB + real-time 6-DoF TCP pose

yubi.description: YUBI (2026) reinvents handheld UMI as a yielding, finger-aligned pinch interface under $200 USD per 3D-printed gripper, eliminating pistol-grip offsets and pairing with high-frequency VR tracking to avoid SLAM frame drops.
highlights: Yielding finger-driven actuation follows natural pinch motion with haptic feedback
Fabricated for under $200 USD per gripper with 3D-printed parts
High-frequency VR tracking avoids monocular ORB-SLAM3 frame drops
Sharpened fingertip geometry excels at cable insertion and box assembly

specs.tracking_method: Integrated high-frequency VR tracking (Meta Quest controllers)
specs.sensors: VR pose tracking + finger-aligned mechanism + stationary VR camera rig
specs.robot_free: Yes, portable and stationary desktop modes
specs.output_data: High-precision 6-DoF pose + natural pinch aperture + vision

dexumi.description: DexUMI extends robot-free UMI collection to multi-finger dexterous hands via an ~850 g wearable exoskeleton recording 6–12 DoF finger motion and wrist vision, used in cross-embodiment pretraining for models like NVIDIA GR00T 2.
highlights: Extends robot-free UMI capture from parallel grippers to dexterous hands
Supports 6 to 12 DoF wearable mapping at ~850 g weight
Used in NVIDIA GR00T 2 pretraining for dexterous hand skill transfer
Mitigates human-to-robot kinematic retargeting mismatch

specs.tracking_method: Wrist visual-inertial SLAM + wearable joint encoders
specs.output_data: 6-DoF wrist trajectory + multi-finger joint actions + wrist vision

dexcap.description: DexCap from Stanford is a portable dexterous mocap system kept under a $4,000 USD budget, combining mocap gloves, wrist SLAM and a chest-mounted RGB-D camera vest to capture 3D point clouds and finger motions without external MoCap studios.
highlights: Total system cost kept under $4,000 USD without external optical MoCap
Occlusion-robust finger tracking synchronized with palm SLAM
Reuses the exact chest camera viewpoint on the robot to ease domain transfer
Supports human-in-the-loop correction to boost success on complex tasks

specs.tracking_method: Wrist SLAM + electromagnetic/mocap glove finger tracking
specs.sensors: Chest RGB-D camera vest + bimanual mocap gloves + wrist tracking
specs.output_data: RGB-D point clouds + 6-DoF wrist pose + fine finger joints

meta-project-aria.description: Meta Project Aria is the leading egocentric multimodal research glasses platform (~75 g). Equipped with factory-calibrated global-shutter SLAM cameras, RGB, eye tracking and dual high-rate IMUs, it powers EgoExo4D and EgoMimic robot learning.
highlights: Weighs ~74–76 g with rigid factory calibration and <0.4% open-loop trajectory drift
Gen 2 upgrades to 4 global-shutter 120dB HDR CV cameras with 80° stereo overlap
Powers foundational egocentric datasets including EgoExo4D and EgoMimic
Dual high-rate IMUs (800/1000 Hz) with hardware timestamp synchronization

specs.tracking_method: Multi-camera global-shutter SLAM + dual high-rate IMUs (800/1000 Hz)
specs.sensors: Gen 2: 4x global-shutter CV cameras (120dB HDR) + RGB + eye tracking + dual IMU + 7 mics
specs.output_data: High-precision 6-DoF head pose + egocentric RGB/SLAM + gaze/audio

robocap.description: RoboCap (Oct 2026) is an egocentric robot-learning capture platform integrating 6 near-field cameras and dual IMUs into a 250 g hat, paired with the Grounded API for centimeter-accurate 3D hand tracking and depth estimation.
highlights: 250 g hat with 6 cameras arranged specifically for near-field bimanual manipulation
Vertically integrated hardware + Grounded API for cm-level 3D hand and depth tracking
Lighter and less socially intrusive than VR/MR headsets (Vision Pro / Quest 3)
Purpose-built for scalable in-the-wild egocentric robot data collection

specs.target_embodiment: General bimanual and humanoid hand manipulation
specs.output_data: cm-level 3D hand tracking + dense depth + 6-DoF head SLAM

mobile-aloha-teleop.description: Mobile ALOHA is Stanford's open-source whole-body mobile bimanual teleoperation platform (~$32,000 full system). Operators drive a mobile base and twin leader arms to control identical follower arms, yielding 100% embodiment-matched data.
highlights: Isomorphic leader-follower arms eliminate kinematic retargeting error
Full open-source system at ~$32,000 (mobile base, 4 arms, onboard compute/power)
Learns complex bimanual household tasks from dozens of demos with ACT
Catalyzed the open-source bimanual imitation learning ecosystem

specs.tracking_method: Isomorphic leader-arm joint encoders + mobile base linkage
specs.sensors: Dual wrist cameras + front camera + 4-arm joint encoders
specs.output_data: 50 Hz multi-view RGB + 14-DoF joint actions + base velocity

gello.description: GELLO from UC Berkeley is a low-cost (<$300 BoM) 3D-printed teleoperation controller using Dynamixel servos to match the exact kinematics of commercial arms like Franka, UR5 and xArm.
highlights: Single-arm BoM under $300 USD compared to $30k+ robot-to-robot teleop
Matches exact kinematics of commercial arms (Franka, UR5, xArm)
Outperforms VR controllers and 3D spacemouses in operator intuition and speed
Compact, portable and fully open-source hardware and software
applications: Low-cost teleoperation of commercial robot arms

specs.tracking_method: Direct joint-angle readout via scaled Dynamixel leader arm
specs.sensors: Dynamixel joint encoders (no external cameras required)
specs.robot_free: No, connected to target follower arm
specs.target_embodiment: Franka, UR5, xArm and other commercial arms
specs.output_data: High-precision joint angle trajectories + gripper command
